name: Connector Pinout Library
blurb: pin maps of USB-C, SWD, JTAG, JST, IDC and other common connectors
intro: Pin maps of common board connectors, transcribed from each connector's standard or owner document, with the view (which side pin 1 is seen from) stated. Pick a connector, or search all of them for a signal name.

examples.title: Where is SWDIO on each debug header

usage: Give a connector id (usbc, usbc2, usba, usbmicro, swd10, jtag20, tc2030, avrisp, ftdi6, qwiic, grove, rpi40, pmod, rj45, db9rs232, db9can, hdmi, microsd, or all) and optionally a search text matched against pin, signal and function. It returns the pin table, the pitch and the view pin 1 is seen from, plus design notes (e.g. Rd on CC). Use it when drawing a symbol or wiring a debug/IO header; for JST/IDC housings it explains that pin meaning comes from the schematic.
sources: USB Type-C Cable and Connector Specification R2.x; USB 2.0 and USB 3.2 specifications
ARM DUI 0499 / Keil Cortex Debug connectors; SEGGER UM08001; Tag-Connect TC2030-CTX
Raspberry Pi GPIO documentation; SparkFun Qwiic; Seeed Grove; Digilent Pmod spec v1.3.1
TIA-568, TIA-574, CiA 303-1, HDMI 1.4, SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification
